   180	                  [ "str"    <- typeV("str")       ]
   181	                  [ "float"  <- typeV("float")     ], root)
   182	
   183	  // ==== argument/element evaluation: ONE left-to-right loop, tagged by destination ==
   184	  // (list/tuple literals and calls all use it; modules extend ApplyK with their tags)
   185	  syntax ApplyK ::= toCall(Val)
   186	  syntax KItem  ::= #evalArgs(Exprs, Vals, ApplyK)
   187	                  | #evalArgCont(Exprs, Vals, ApplyK)
   188	                  | #applyK(ApplyK, Vals)
   189	  rule <k> #evalArgs((A:Expr, REST:Exprs), ACC:Vals, K:ApplyK) => A ~> #evalArgCont(REST, ACC, K) ... </k>
   190	  rule <k> V:Val ~> #evalArgCont(REST:Exprs, ACC:Vals, K:ApplyK) => #evalArgs(REST, appendVal(ACC, V), K) ... </k>
   191	  rule <k> #evalArgs(.Exprs, ACC:Vals, K:ApplyK) => #applyK(K, ACC) ... </k>
   192	
   193	  // ==== Int / Bool / None literals ==========================================
   194	  rule <k> Int(I:Int)   => I ... </k>
   195	  rule <k> Bool(B:Bool) => B ... </k>
   196	  rule <k> NoneVal      => noneV ... </k>
   197	
   198	  // ==== truthy (If, Assert, BoolOp, IfExp, not, While) ======================
   199	  syntax Bool ::= truthy(Val) [function]
   200	  rule truthy(B:Bool)          => B
   201	  rule truthy(noneV)           => false
   202	  rule truthy(I:Int)           => I =/=Int 0
   203	  rule truthy(str(S:IntSeq))   => notBool (S ==K .IntSeq)
   204	  rule truthy(list(V:ValSeq))  => notBool (V ==K .ValSeq)
   205	  rule truthy(tuple(V:ValSeq)) => notBool (V ==K .ValSeq)
   206	
   207	  // ==== extensible operator dispatch (cases added by the construct modules) ==
   208	  syntax Val  ::= applyUn(String, Val) [function]
   209	  syntax Val  ::= applyBin(String, Val, Val) [function]
   210	  syntax Bool ::= applyCmp(String, Val, Val) [function]
   211	
   212	  // ==== shared list helpers =================================================
   213	  syntax Vals ::= appendVal(Vals, Val) [function, total]
   214	  rule appendVal(.Vals, V:Val)              => V , .Vals
   215	  rule appendVal((V0:Val, VS:Vals), V:Val)  => V0 , appendVal(VS, V)
   216	
   217	  syntax ValSeq ::= vals2valSeq(Vals) [function, total]
   218	  rule vals2valSeq(.Vals)            => .ValSeq
   219	  rule vals2valSeq((V:Val, VS:Vals)) => vCons(V, vals2valSeq(VS))
   220	
   221	  // ==== shared sequence length (len / summaries across many modules) ========
   222	  // (positional access valSeqAt/intSeqAt + normIdx live in subscript.k)

   225	  rule vsLen(vCons(_:Val, S:ValSeq)) => 1 +Int vsLen(S)

   231	  // in-bounds positional write (list subscript-assign); OOB leaves the seq unchanged
   232	  // (valid programs write in-bounds — mirrors valSeqAt's total-but-underspecified stance)
   233	  syntax ValSeq ::= setVSAt(ValSeq, Int, Val) [function, total]
   234	  rule setVSAt(.ValSeq, _:Int, _:Val)               => .ValSeq
   235	  rule setVSAt(vCons(_:Val, S:ValSeq), 0, V:Val)    => vCons(V, S)

     1	// reference/src/semantics/operators.k — MPY-OPERATORS
     2	// The operator DISPATCH layer: operands evaluate by strictness (heat/cool over KResult=Val),
     3	// the cooled node hands to applyUn/applyBin/applyCmp (declared in core.k; each domain file
     4	// owns its cases — bool.k, int.k, float.k, str.k, list.k, tuple.k, set.k, dict.k).
     5	
     6	module MPY-OPERATORS
     7	  imports MPY-CORE
     8	  imports MPY-ITER
     9	
    10	  rule <k> UnaryOp(OP:String, V:Val) => applyUn(OP, V) ... </k>
    11	
    12	  rule <k> BinOp(OP:String, L:Val, R:Val) => applyBin(OP, L, R) ... </k>
    13	
    14	  // Compare's right operand sits under the CmpOp wrapper — contexts instead of attributes
    15	  context Compare(HOLE, _)
    16	  context Compare(_:Val, CmpOp(_, HOLE))
    17	  rule <k> Compare(LV:Val, CmpOp(OP:String, RV:Val)) => applyCmp(OP, LV, RV) ... </k> [owise]
    18	
    19	  rule applyCmp("is",     V:Val, noneV) => V ==K noneV
    20	  rule applyCmp("is not", V:Val, noneV) => notBool (V ==K noneV)
    21	
    22	  // ==== operand deref: heap objects combine/compare by STRUCTURE ============
    23	  // (Python: list == is structural; identity only via `is`.) priority(40)
    24	  // preempts the generic dispatch so applyUn/applyBin/applyCmp never see a ref.
    25	  rule <k> BinOp(OP:String, ref(H:Int), R:Expr) => BinOp(OP, V, R) ... </k>
    26	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
    27	       [priority(40)]
    28	  rule <k> BinOp(OP:String, L:Val, ref(H:Int)) => BinOp(OP, L, V) ... </k>
    29	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
    30	       requires notBool isRefV(L)
    31	       [priority(40)]
    32	
    33	  // the left operand of `in`/`not in` is an ELEMENT (compares by ==K) — never deref'd
    34	  rule <k> Compare(ref(H:Int), CmpOp(OP:String, R:Expr)) => Compare(V, CmpOp(OP, R)) ... </k>
    35	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
    36	       requires OP =/=String "in" andBool OP =/=String "not in"
    37	       [priority(40)]
    38	  rule <k> Compare(L:Val, CmpOp(OP:String, ref(H:Int))) => Compare(L, CmpOp(OP, V)) ... </k>
    39	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
    40	       requires notBool isRefV(L)
    41	        orBool OP ==String "in" orBool OP ==String "not in"
    42	       [priority(40)]
    43	
    44	  rule <k> UnaryOp(OP:String, ref(H:Int)) => UnaryOp(OP, V) ... </k>
    45	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
    46	       [priority(40)]
    47	endmodule

     1	// reference/src/semantics/int.k — MPY-INT
     2	// Int cases of the operator dispatch; Python // and % are floored (pyMod).
     3	
     4	module MPY-INT
     5	  imports MPY-CORE
     6	
     7	  rule applyUn("-", I:Int) => 0 -Int I
     8	
     9	  rule applyBin("+",  I1:Int, I2:Int) => I1 +Int I2
    10	  // Bool participates in int arithmetic (x += (a == b))
    11	  rule applyBin("+",  I:Int, B:Bool) => I +Int #if B #then 1 #else 0 #fi
    12	  rule applyBin("+",  B:Bool, I:Int) => #if B #then 1 #else 0 #fi +Int I
    13	  rule applyBin("-",  I1:Int, I2:Int) => I1 -Int I2
    14	  rule applyBin("*",  I1:Int, I2:Int) => I1 *Int I2
    15	  rule applyBin("%",  I1:Int, I2:Int) => pyMod(I1, I2)
    16	  rule applyBin("//", I1:Int, I2:Int) => (I1 -Int pyMod(I1, I2)) /Int I2
    17	  rule applyBin("**", I1:Int, I2:Int) => I1 ^Int I2 requires I2 >=Int 0
    18	
    19	  syntax Int ::= pyMod(Int, Int) [function]
    20	  rule pyMod(I1:Int, I2:Int) => ((I1 %Int I2) +Int I2) %Int I2
    21	
    22	  rule applyCmp("<",  I1:Int, I2:Int)   => I1 <Int  I2
    23	  rule applyCmp("<=", I1:Int, I2:Int)   => I1 <=Int I2
    24	  rule applyCmp(">",  I1:Int, I2:Int)   => I1 >Int  I2
    25	  rule applyCmp(">=", I1:Int, I2:Int)   => I1 >=Int I2
    26	  rule applyCmp("==", I1:Int, I2:Int)   => I1 ==Int I2
    27	  rule applyCmp("!=", I1:Int, I2:Int)   => I1 =/=Int I2

     1	// reference/src/semantics/bool.k — MPY-BOOL
     2	// Bool operator cases + the truthy boolean operations (not / and / or; and-or are

     5	module MPY-BOOL
     6	  imports MPY-CORE
     7	
     8	  rule applyUn("not", V:Val) => notBool truthy(V)
     9	
    10	  rule applyCmp("==", B1:Bool, B2:Bool) => B1 ==Bool B2
    11	  rule applyCmp("!=", B1:Bool, B2:Bool) => B1 =/=Bool B2
    12	
    13	  // ==== BoolOp: short-circuit, value-returning and / or =====================
    14	  // the node is its own accumulator: heat the HEAD element only, then either return it
    15	  // (short-circuit) or drop it and continue
    16	  context BoolOp(_, (HOLE:Expr, _:Exprs))
    17	  rule <k> BoolOp(_:String, (V:Val, .Exprs)) => V ... </k>
    18	  rule <k> BoolOp("and", (V:Val, A:Expr, REST:Exprs)) => BoolOp("and", (A, REST)) ... </k>
    19	       requires truthy(V)
    20	  rule <k> BoolOp("and", (V:Val, _:Expr, _:Exprs)) => V ... </k>
    21	       requires notBool truthy(V)
    22	  rule <k> BoolOp("or",  (V:Val, _:Expr, _:Exprs)) => V ... </k>
    23	       requires truthy(V)
    24	  rule <k> BoolOp("or",  (V:Val, A:Expr, REST:Exprs)) => BoolOp("or", (A, REST)) ... </k>
    25	       requires notBool truthy(V)
    26	
    27	  // ==== heap-object head: decide truthiness THROUGH the heap, never rewrite the
    28	  // operand — and/or return the OBJECT itself (Python identity), not its structure
    29	  rule <k> BoolOp(_:String, (ref(H:Int), .Exprs)) => ref(H) ... </k>
    30	       [priority(40)]
    31	  rule <k> BoolOp("and", (ref(H:Int), A:Expr, REST:Exprs)) => BoolOp("and", (A, REST)) ... </k>
    32	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
    33	       requires truthy(V)
    34	       [priority(40)]
    35	  rule <k> BoolOp("and", (ref(H:Int), _:Expr, _:Exprs)) => ref(H) ... </k>
    36	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
    37	       requires notBool truthy(V)
    38	       [priority(40)]
    39	  rule <k> BoolOp("or", (ref(H:Int), _:Expr, _:Exprs)) => ref(H) ... </k>
    40	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
    41	       requires truthy(V)
    42	       [priority(40)]
    43	  rule <k> BoolOp("or", (ref(H:Int), A:Expr, REST:Exprs)) => BoolOp("or", (A, REST)) ... </k>
    44	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
    45	       requires notBool truthy(V)
    46	       [priority(40)]
    47	endmodule

     1	// reference/src/semantics/functions.k — MPY-FUNCTIONS
     2	
     3	module MPY-FUNCTIONS
     4	  imports MPY-CORE
     5	
     6	  // call routing + callee/arg evaluation (#callee/#args/#argCont) live in call.k;
     7	  // this module owns the frame lifecycle (bind params, return, pop).
     8	  syntax KItem ::= frame(continuation: K, callerEnv: Int, savedLoc: Int)
     9	                 | #bindP(ParamNames, Vals)
    10	                 | "#pop"
    11	                 | "#endcall"
    12	
    13	  // ==== def / anonymous closure =============================================
    14	  rule <k> FuncDef(F:String, Params(PNS:ParamNames), BODY:Stmts) => .K ... </k>
    15	       <env> L:Int </env>
    16	       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map => M [ F <- closureVal(PNS, BODY, L) ], _) ... </scopes>
    17	
    18	  syntax Expr ::= closureExpr(ParamNames, Stmts)
    19	  rule <k> closureExpr(PNS:ParamNames, BODY:Stmts) => closureVal(PNS, BODY, L) ... </k>
    20	       <env> L:Int </env>
    21	
    22	  // ==== annotated def/lambda (closure cells; spec 2.3) ======================
    23	  // closureValC(params, cellvars, body, captured-cells). No frame anchor: all
    24	  // enclosing-local reads are freevars (symtable-complete) and go through the
    25	  // captured cells; everything else is global/builtin, so the callee frame's
    26	  // parent is the module scope (0) — sound after the defining frame dies.
    27	  syntax Val ::= closureValC(ParamNames, ParamNames, Stmts, Map)
    28	
    29	  // capture: resolve each freevar to the enclosing frame's cellRef, then bind
    30	  // (FuncDef) or yield (Lambda) the closure value.
    31	  syntax KItem ::= #mkClosure(String, ParamNames, ParamNames, ParamNames, Stmts, Map)
    32	                 | #mkLambda(ParamNames, ParamNames, ParamNames, Stmts, Map)

*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: /audit-output/REVIEW.md
+# Independent adversarial audit: 138-is-equal-to-sum-even
+
+The candidate contains a legitimate, result-constraining partial-correctness
+proof for the submitted integer program under the supplied semantics. I assign
+`CONCERNS / LEGIT`, rather than `PASS / LEGIT`, because the requested generation
+metadata is absent and the last bridge from the proved parity/threshold formula
+to the English “sum of exactly four positive even numbers” remains an elementary
+informal mathematical argument rather than a K theorem. Neither limitation
+allows a false program result to be proved.
+
+All candidate inputs were treated as untrusted. Candidate files were copied to
+`/tmp/audit-work/review-138`; no candidate-built definition or cache was copied
+or used. Reviewer scripts, mutations, and bounded command logs are in
+`/audit-output/evidence/`.
+
+## 1. Input and provenance integrity
+
+Semantics mode is `SUPPLIED_SEMANTICS`. The trusted
+`/reference/reference-semantics` tree exists, so there is no rendered-mode/mount
+contradiction and no infrastructure breach.
+
+The recursive file/type inventory contains no symlinks in either semantics
+tree. `diff -qr --no-dereference` reports no missing, additional, changed, or
+mistyped entry between the candidate and trusted semantics (exit 0). The
+candidate prompt and translator are byte-identical to their trusted mounts
+(both `cmp` commands exit 0):
+
+| Artifact | Trusted/candidate SHA-256 |
+|---|---|
+| `prompt.py` | `e49218abe89b2b138512731659d96115b045637b8cebe43d2407656209332e58` |
+| `py2mpy.py` | `406485eac118431c08ef59f30f79dfa6aa9d5825408917fc5ce7c806e664db16` |
+
+Full commands, types, hashes, and statuses are in
+[`evidence/provenance.log`](evidence/provenance.log), generated by
+[`evidence/check_provenance.sh`](evidence/check_provenance.sh).
+
+The following requested provenance artifacts are absent from `/candidate`;
+each `test -f` exited 1:
+
+- `run-input.json`
+- `metrics.json`
+- `codex-last.txt`
+- `codex-output.log`
+
+No top-level structured generation trace (`*trace*` or `*.jsonl`) is present.
+There is also no candidate `PROOF.md` or candidate vacuity spec. These absences
+limit provenance/audit history, but they do not remove a source, semantics,
+specification, or positive claim needed for independent execution. Candidate
+`.pyc` files and concrete-test files were not trusted or used to reconstruct
+the proof.
+
+Stage result: integrity of every executable source used by the proof passes;
+generation-history completeness has a documented concern.
+
+## 2. Program fidelity and candidate-versus-canonical checks
+
+### Contract and implementation
+
+The trusted prompt asks whether integer-like input `n` can be expressed as the
+sum of exactly four positive even integers and gives `4 -> False`, `6 -> False`,
+and `8 -> True`. The trusted canonical implementation returns:
+
+```python
+n % 2 == 0 and n >= 8
+```
+
+The submitted implementation returns:
+
+```python
+n >= 8 and n % 2 == 0
+```
+
+For mathematical integers these differ only in short-circuit order and are
+extensionally equal. The proof's formal domain is K `Int`, so it does not claim
+behavior for floats, strings, or other Python objects. It is stronger than any
+positive-integer restriction because it covers every mathematical integer.
+
+### Trusted retranslation
+
+Running
+
+```text
+python3 /reference/py2mpy.py solution.py > regenerated-solution.mpy
+cmp -s regenerated-solution.mpy solution.mpy
+```
+
+from scratch exits 0 for both commands. Both files hash to
+`4be6b3778909ca1c91506046bb2f1925cb4f689dad0162b5f8faa007e84eee8d`.
+See [`evidence/fidelity.log`](evidence/fidelity.log) and
+[`evidence/check_translation.sh`](evidence/check_translation.sh).
+
+### Independent differential
+
+[`evidence/differential_test.py`](evidence/differential_test.py) imports the
+trusted canonical entry point and the scratch copy of the submitted entry point
+independently. It checks:
+
+- documented examples `4, 6, 8`;
+- the exact threshold and parity boundaries around 8;
+- negative, zero, small, 100-digit, and nearby values;
+- every integer from -256 through 256;
+- 500 deterministic signed integers of up to 512 bits (seed 138);
+- the zero-argument call boundary, where both raise the same `TypeError`.
+
+There were 1,007 unique integer inputs and zero mismatches. The command exited
+0. The exact deterministic input construction and results are in
+[`evidence/fidelity.log`](evidence/fidelity.log). This is finite evidence, not
+a universal proof.
+
+Stage result: pass.
+
+## 3. Clean proof reconstruction
+
+I copied only `solution.py`, `solution.mpy`, `spec.k`, `verification.k`, and the
+source semantics tree into the scratch directory. No `*-kompiled` directory or
+candidate cache was copied.
+
+The available toolchain was K `v7.1.337` (build date 2026-06-18). The fresh
+Haskell definition was built with:
+
+```text
+kompile verification.k --backend haskell \
+  --main-module VERIFICATION --syntax-module VERIFICATION \
+  --output-definition verification-kompiled
+```
+
+It exited 0. See
+[`evidence/build-verification.log`](evidence/build-verification.log).
+
+The original specification and every one of its four positive claims were then
+run independently:
+
+| Target | Command suffix | Result |
+|---|---|---|
+| all candidate claims | `kprove spec.k --definition verification-kompiled --spec-module SPEC` | `#Top`, exit 0 |
+| universal result | `kprove spec-main.k ... --spec-module SPEC-MAIN` | `#Top`, exit 0 |
+| true branch | `kprove spec-true.k ... --spec-module SPEC-TRUE` | `#Top`, exit 0 |
+| below-eight branch | `kprove spec-low.k ... --spec-module SPEC-LOW` | `#Top`, exit 0 |
+| nonzero-remainder branch | `kprove spec-nonzero.k ... --spec-module SPEC-NONZERO` | `#Top`, exit 0 |
+
+The exact reconstruction script is
+[`evidence/rebuild_and_prove.sh`](evidence/rebuild_and_prove.sh); bounded logs
+are `evidence/prove-{all,main,true,low,nonzero}.log`.
+
+As a stronger independent pinning check, I built a second Haskell definition
+from `reference-semantics/semantics.k` with main module `MPY`, without importing
+`verification.k`. The reviewer-authored
+[`evidence/spec-fixed-real-program.k`](evidence/spec-fixed-real-program.k)
+loads the exact submitted `Module(FuncDef(...))`, resolves
+`is_equal_to_sum_even` from the module scope, calls it for arbitrary `N:Int`,
+and targets the parity/threshold formula. It also closed with `#Top`, exit 0.
+See [`evidence/build-fixed-semantics.log`](evidence/build-fixed-semantics.log)
+and
+[`evidence/prove-fixed-real-program.log`](evidence/prove-fixed-real-program.log).
+
+For concrete semantics evidence, I independently translated a five-witness
+program, built a fresh LLVM `MPY-KRUN` definition, and ran it. `krun` ended with
+`.K`, `NoExc`, and exit-code 0. The module scope retained the exact expected
+closure AST. Commands and output are in
+[`evidence/concrete-witnesses-summary.log`](evidence/concrete-witnesses-summary.log).
+
+The compiler emitted only unused-variable warnings in `str.k` during Haskell
+builds. The LLVM build additionally warned about non-exhaustive total helper
+matches in unused map/string/float/subscript helpers; none is reachable from
+this program or its proof. These warnings are accounted for in Stages 5 and 7.
+
+Stage result: pass.
+
+## 4. Adequacy and real-program pinning
+
+### Claims in plain language
+
+All four claims start from the same realizable state: environment location 0,
+an empty module scope whose parent is the supplied builtins scope, allocation
+locations 1 and 0, empty heap and stack, no pending return or exception, and
+exit code 0.
+
+1. Universal claim: for every mathematical integer `N`, the returned Boolean
+   equals `N >= 8 and pyMod(N, 2) == 0`.
+2. True corollary: when `N >= 8` and its remainder modulo 2 is zero, return
+   `true`.
+3. Low corollary: when `N < 8`, return `false`.
+4. Odd/nonzero-remainder corollary: when `N >= 8` and its remainder modulo 2 is
+   nonzero, return `false`.
+
+The preconditions are satisfiable. The reviewer witnesses are respectively
+`N=8`, `N=8`, `N=7`, and `N=9`. For each, the trusted canonical, submitted
+Python function, main K formula, and claimed result agree. Exact output is in
+[`evidence/concrete-witnesses-summary.log`](evidence/concrete-witnesses-summary.log),
+and the independent witness checker is
+[`evidence/claim_witnesses.py`](evidence/claim_witnesses.py).
+
+### Pinning and control flow
+
+`verification.k` adds one fresh entry syntax item and one rule. The rule does
+not replace the function result with a summary or oracle. It rewrites the fresh
+entry item to a normal supplied-semantics `Call` of a closure whose parameter,
+body, return, Boolean operation, comparisons, modulo expression, constants, and
+definition environment are exactly the normalized submitted `solution.mpy`
+AST. Its `...` preserves any trailing continuation and every configuration cell
+is framed unchanged.
+
+The direct closure harness deliberately omits the module-level function-name
+binding. That omission cannot influence this body: its only lookup is local
+parameter `n`. The bridge-free real-module proof in Stage 3 independently
+executes `#loadAll`, the actual `FuncDef` binding, name lookup, and the same call
+for arbitrary `N`, obtaining the same formula using only supplied semantics.
+Thus the harness is pinned to the real submitted function rather than a
+substituted algorithm.
+
+There are no loop or helper claims. The function body itself executes:
+callee and argument evaluation, frame allocation, parameter binding, local name
+lookup, short-circuit `and`, integer comparison, modulo, equality, `Return`,
+frame pop, and state restoration all use supplied semantic rules.
+
+The target is result-constraining: the universal target is a specific Boolean
+formula in `N`, and each corollary targets a concrete Boolean. It is neither a
+free variable, tautology, nor one-way implication.
+
+Stage result: pass.
+
+## 5. Rule-by-rule static soundness review
+
+### Exhaustive inventory
+
+[`evidence/rule-inventory.txt`](evidence/rule-inventory.txt), generated by
+[`evidence/make_rule_inventory.sh`](evidence/make_rule_inventory.sh), records
+every source syntax/declaration line, rule start, context, configuration, claim,
+guard, semantic attribute, priority, opaque/trust marker, and source hash. It
+contains 1,477 lines and is the exhaustive searchable inventory. Across the
+supplied semantics and `verification.k` there are 228 syntax-declaration lines,
+696 ordinary rule starts, five explicit contexts, one configuration, and 50
+priority annotations. There are no `[functional]` declarations and no
+`[simplification]` rules. The inventory separately captures all `[function]`,
+`[total]`, `[concrete]`, `[owise]`, macro, strictness, symbol, and
+`no-evaluators` attributes. `spec.k` adds four claims and no rules.
+
+Per-file decision:
+
+| File | Syntax | Rules | Static decision |
+|---|---:|---:|---|
+| `semantics.k` | 0 | 0 | Import aggregator only; exact trusted tree. |
+| `semantics/syntax.k` | 16 | 0 | AST declarations. Used productions match the submitted MPY; unused productions are inert. |
+| `semantics/core.k` | 37 | 46 | Configuration, literals, scope/name lookup, sequencing, argument evaluation, and helpers are coherent on the used path. Unused allocation/cell/list helpers do not match. |
+| `semantics/operators.k` | 0 | 10 | Used generic unary/binary/compare dispatch and evaluation contexts preserve order. Reference-dereference priority rules cannot match integer operands. |
+| `semantics/int.k` | 1 | 16 | Used `>=`, `%`, `==`, and `pyMod(_,2)` rules implement ordinary integer mathematics/Python positive-divisor modulo. Other operator cases are sort/operator-disjoint. |
+| `semantics/bool.k` | 0 | 13 | Used head context and guarded `and` rules are disjoint (`truthy` versus its negation), short-circuit correctly, and return the operand value. Reference cases cannot match. |
+| `semantics/functions.k` | 4 | 15 | Used ordinary `FuncDef`, parameter bind, `Return`, end-call, and pop rules preserve binding, return, stack, environment, and scope allocation. Annotated-cell closure rules cannot match. |
+| `semantics/call.k` | 3 | 21 | Generic call evaluates callee then arguments; the ordinary closure rule creates/restores the exact frame. Builtin, method, type, heap, and annotated-closure dispatch is disjoint. |
+| `semantics/assert.k` | 0 | 3 | Unused by the proof; used only in independent concrete smoke evidence. Supplied baseline. |
+| `semantics/builtins.k` | 38 | 137 | No builtin call occurs. All patterns are unreachable from the submitted AST. Supplied baseline; opaque MD5 primitive unused. |
+| `semantics/comprehension.k` | 3 | 7 | No comprehension syntax occurs; inert. |
+| `semantics/concrete.k` | 5 | 16 | Not imported by proof module `MPY`; cannot contribute to any `#Top`. Used only by LLVM smoke execution. |
+| `semantics/controls.k` | 3 | 34 | No assignment/if/loop/break/continue syntax occurs; inert. |
+| `semantics/dict.k` | 12 | 28 | No dictionary value, expression, call, or method occurs; type/head-disjoint. |
+| `semantics/float.k` | 34 | 121 | No float syntax/value occurs. Float dispatch is sort-disjoint from K `Int`; all opaque float symbols are unused. |
+| `semantics/iter.k` | 1 | 0 | Iterator marker declaration only; unused. |
+| `semantics/list.k` | 5 | 27 | No list/ref syntax or value occurs; type/head-disjoint. |
+| `semantics/methods.k` | 27 | 75 | No attribute or method call occurs; inert. |
+| `semantics/range.k` | 2 | 6 | No range or iteration occurs; inert. |
